labels.name: ✅ accepted-PRs-welcome

items.body:
### Provide environment information

```
  System:
    OS: macOS 13.2.1
    CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M2 Max
    Memory: 57.83 GB / 96.00 GB
    Shell: 5.8.1 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 18.15.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.15.0/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.19 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.15.0/bin/yarn
    npm: 9.5.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.15.0/bin/npm
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 112.0.5615.137
    Safari: 16.3
```

```
"@trpc/server": "10.23.0",
```

### Describe the bug

routers don't seem to check the types of their procedures or sub-routers. self contained example:

```ts
import {initTRPC} from '@trpc/server'
import {createNextApiHandler} from '@trpc/server/adapters/next'

const trpca = initTRPC.context<{a: string}>().create()
const trpcb = initTRPC.context<{b: string}>().create()

const parent = trpca.router({
  a: trpca.procedure.query(({ctx}) => ctx.a.slice()),
  b: trpcb.procedure.query(({ctx}) => ctx.b.slice()),
})

export default createNextApiHandler({
  router: parent,
  createContext: () => ({a: 'aaa'}),
})
```

this is fine at compile time, and hitting `/api/trpc.a` works, but hitting `/api/trpc.b` gets `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice')` (since `ctx.b` is never defined anywhere) - I shouldn't have been allowed to use `trpcb.procedure.query(...)` on a router for `trpca`, since they have different contexts.

### Link to reproduction

https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?ts=5.0.3#code/JYWwDg9gTgLgBAb2AO2DAKgJQAoGEC+cAZlBCHAOQACMUYAxgPQDOAplAG7sUBQoksRPSisAhjFYA5VgA8YAQTDAAEqOQATADbtCJMpRp0mbTu0aj1osBKjNGyWTF496EZM3i0GouAF44KGhYeAB0rsgScgA8CKIAXHAeUCgA5vgAfAAUAJRhIuKsOS5uHnBe9ABGfgGoGDi4YW6RMDEVCUmpGTl5YhJFxe7wYKIiEdXloiGkAK42mQg8cHDxZUaTYKT0rOrTIiEAjtPsAJ6Z8-QwMvjZfulwFzIhk8yawFs52QA0i3BtqwwVEIbCBbHZ7Q4nM4IB7XW73S4hQEvN6FbJfHjXHg8WQCeDqVhEUTTTTwYS9KSORQqNRadjzH4zGwJYajGDfJZkgq4JqOBI5OHzFYUUQiijXb7XIA

### To reproduce

Paste the code above into a next api handler. I tried that above using the stackblitz suggested but there's a strange compile error that I don't get locally, it doesn't seem to acknowledge that the export for the next adapter exists: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-qwqz1i-qs9elv?file=src/pages/api/trpc/[trpc].ts

### Additional information

My use-case: I'm trying to make a router in a library, which can be plugged into an application's parent router for modular functionality, with the requirement that the parent has a context which meets the requirement of the library router. But the type system doesn't seem to enforce this. Maybe it's just not supported (yet)?

I'm putting yes I'd be down to fix this but I don't know if I'll have the time to so if someone else wants to, go for it!

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR fixing this bug!

<sub>[TRP-29](https://linear.app/trpc/issue/TRP-29/bug-conflicting-ctx-types-allowed-at-compile-time)</sub>

items.title: Add experimental procedure extensions API
items.body:
Closes #4191 

#4191 requests a way for a middleware to extend a baseProcedure with some required input data

ALSO we would _love_ to make it easier for 3rd party vendors such as authentication, authorisation, logging, crashlytics, analytics, etc, tools to provide 1-line integrations without knowing _anything about the contents of `t`_ (which is currently impossible

ALSO we would love for monorepo owners to be able to write middlewares in a completely `t` agnostic way, for the same reasons of separation as 3rd parties _need_ that agnostic behaviour to write anything

This PR adds `createProcedureExtension` which can be used to create an extension function, receiving the ProcedureBuilder as an input and being permitted to make whatever changes it likes. Some early thoughts:

* This is a powerful API and may be subject to misuse and anti-patterns, but also opens a whole new world of 3rd party integrations up to us
* This API exposes many builder methods which we have no proven use case for currently, should we Pick<T> the methods we actually want to expose? How would that work with the builder API?
* What happens if an input is an array and the extension wants to add an object to it? (and vice versa)
* What about meta? Should be enable the extending of the meta type from a chained `.meta` call? Might open some additional doors here but isn't currently a feature of tRPC although both input and context can do it.

## 🎯 Changes

What changes are made in this PR? Is it a feature or a bug fix?

- [ ] If necessary, I have added documentation related to the changes made.

items.title: Middleware: swap context

labels.name: 🧙🏻  typescript wizardry
labels.description: if you want a typescript-challenge, look at these

items.body:
From #818 

@KATT I created a new PR because I made a lot of (type-level) changes.

- Added TInputContext to Router and Procedure
- Tests to make sure context-swapping works and doesn't have unexpected side-effects
- Removed swapContext method for now - can be added later, but the use-case is supported via `return next({ ctx: ... })`
- Replaced `MiddlewareFunctionKeepContext` and `MiddlewareFunctionSwapContext` with a single `MiddlewareFunction` type with an overloaded `next` input
- Made `next({ ctx: ... })` a function which can pass anything to `ctx`. The type passed is inferred as the `TContext` for the middleware's return value - this gets the `expectTypeOf` test added in the previous PR working
- Removed a bunch of ` = any` in type args. It was hard to keep track of what needed to be changed when defaults were used. I don't think any were internal so I've left them like that, but worth taking a look
- Added a swap-context example to the docs

Notes for the future:

- The types in `procedure.ts` are a bit loose. It's internal, so that's ok as long as it's covered by tests, but I think the crux is that it uses a `middlewares` array. I haven't tried this at all, but I think we could get more type safety by requiring that a procedure has exactly one middleware, and adding some helpers which compose middlewares. That way we can properly keep track of input and output contexts, instead of procedures having a list of unknown -> unknown middlewares.
- Having `ProcedureWithInput` and `ProcedureWithoutInput` made this a bit harder than it feels like it should be. Maybe Procedure instances could always have inputs, where for convenience you can add queries/mutations/subscriptions to a router without, but the "input" defaults to `() => undefined` (which is a valid `ProcedureInputParserCustomValidatorEsque`, I believe)
- When classes/interfaces start having loads of generics like here, something I've tried before is to have a single generic with properties, so you can do something like `class Router<T extends TRouterOptions>{ ... }`. Then to get the context you do `T['context']`, to get queries it'd be `T['queries']`. This can make it easier to write helper functions and refactor things without having to duplicate the ever-growing `<TInputContext, TContext, TQueries, TMutations, TSubscriptions, TGodKnowsWhatElse>` typearg lists, or fall back on potentially dangerous `any` defaults.

I am currently writing an API with trpc, and I am using `ctx` to pass down a user object once an auth header is being sent to the server. However, I am always falling back to using `ctx.user!.id` because the user attribute *can be* (but not must be) `null`/`undefined`.

Is there a way to strictly typing the context for specific routers?

I'd love to see a solution for typing the context for different behaviors. Or at least, when there is a middleware, and the middleware is checking for existence of any context variable, so that the context is being "re-typed" with the checked presence in the middleware.

As written above, I am currently using `ctx.user!.id`, which **is working**, but is not ideal.

Different types of `middlewareMarker`
items.body:
Hello,

We have two separate folder for backend and frontend in our repo (no workspace setup) as they are compiled in their respective directories.

In an attempt to introduce `trpc` I stumbled upon an issue that we have two copies of `@trpc/server` package - both in server's and in client's `node_modules`.
The problem is that when I import `AppRouter` type from the server to client - I get a type mismatch of the `middlewareMarker` which is a symbol created in [middlewares.ts](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/4c91e920529daa4f7c1a88cbc7b0db8a5ed405ce/packages/server/src/internals/middlewares.ts#L4).
It seems like I have two symbols that are by definition different.

Is it intended to be so?
Do I have to migrate to common `node_modules` (via workspaces) or there is a way around it?

The code:
```ts
// backend/index.ts
import * as trpc from "trpc/server";

const router = trpc.router();
export type AppRouter = typeof router;
```

```ts
// frontend/index.ts
import {createReactQueryHooks} from "@trpc/react";
import type { AppRouter } from "../backend/index";

export const trpc = createReactQueryHooks<AppRouter>();
```

The error:
```ts
(property) BaseHandlerOptions<AnyRouter<any>, e.Request<ParamsDictionary, any, any, QueryString.ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>>.router: AnyRouter<any>

  The types of '_def.middlewares' are incompatible between these types.

            The types returned by 'next()' are incompatible between these types.

                Type 'MiddlewareResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareResult<Context>'.

                    Type 'MiddlewareOKResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareOKResult<Context>'.
                      Types of property 'marker' are incompatible.
                        Type 'typeof import("/.../backend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker' is not assignable to type 'typeof import("/.../frontend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker'.ts(2322)
```

items.title: feat: pass procedure input to middleware
[RFC] Add middleware `next()`-fn
items.body:
Middlewares will now have to call a `next()` function that you **have to** call.

### Example

> A middleware that measures the time of procedures

```ts
.middleware(async ({ ctx, path, next }) => {
  const start = Date.now()
  await next()
  const end = Date.now()
  console.log({path, took: end - start})
})
```
---

@mmkal @delaneyj - you've both championed this. I really don't like my implementation of the recursive async/await spaghetti, I wrote it in like 5 minutes, but the tests pass and it seems to work. You're both [added as contributors](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/invitations) so you can update the branch directly, would be great if one of you could clean up my implementation.

---

### Todos

- [x] First draft
- [x] Add tests
- [x] Make a prettier implementation
- [x] Update docs
- [x] Update examples

---
Closes #564  #586 #564

items.body:
I've just merged the #732 & #718 to `main` and released a new V9 draft. 

**Are there any other structural, potentially breaking changes that you would want to get into the next major?**

- It should be production-ready so feel free to update your deps to `9.0.0-alpha.4`, play around with it, and give me feedback.
- I have tried slowing down on the major version bumps, so I would ideally not do more breaking changes for a while.
- Planning to release `9.0.0` early next week.
- There _might_ come a `10.x` as well later in a month or so in order to add support for SvelteKit - might require some major changes as their API handlers are a bit different.


> If you're happy you can just give a 👍 on this issue.

## Summary of changes so far

- Middlewares will now have to call a `next()` function that you **have to** call.
- Reduce `TRPCError`s - `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` removed & `PATH_NOT_FOUND` renamed to `NOT_FOUND` (#733)
- Align input and output serialization (#746)
- Remove deprecated `httpErrors`-helper 
- Remove support for `?input` to be an array - now assuming a `Record<number, unknown>`-style dict (changed with backward compat in #669)
- Remove support for `POST` calls being `{ input: x }` (originally from #671)
- 🛬   Incoming as well
